entities.label: Condition
entities.name: Type 2 diabetes
entities.description: Chronic condition of impaired insulin action and secretion leading to high blood glucose.

entities.label: Condition
entities.name: Prediabetes
entities.description: Blood glucose above normal but below the diabetes diagnostic range.

entities.label: Condition
entities.name: Cardiovascular disease
entities.description: Heart and blood vessel disease, the leading cause of death in people with diabetes.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Overweight or obesity
entities.description: BMI of 25 or higher (23 or higher for Asian adults in ADA screening guidance).

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: High blood pressure
entities.description: Blood pressure at or above 130/80 mmHg or treated hypertension.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Older age
entities.description: Risk of type 2 diabetes rises with age; ADA recommends screening all adults from age 35.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Elevated blood glucose
entities.description: Fasting glucose of 100 mg/dL or higher, or A1C of 5.7% or higher.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Physical inactivity
entities.description: Little or no regular physical activity.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Smoking
entities.description: Current tobacco smoking.

entities.label: RiskFactor
entities.name: Family history of diabetes
entities.description: A parent or sibling with diabetes.

entities.label: Test
entities.name: A1C test
entities.description: Average blood glucose over about three months.

entities.label: Test
entities.name: Fasting plasma glucose
entities.description: Blood glucose after at least 8 hours without caloric intake.

entities.label: Test
entities.name: Oral glucose tolerance test
entities.description: Blood glucose 2 hours after a 75 g glucose load.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Structured lifestyle change program
entities.description: Diabetes Prevention Program style coaching on diet, activity and weight.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Modest weight loss
entities.description: Losing 5 to 7 percent of body weight.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: 150 minutes of moderate activity per week
entities.description: Moderate-intensity aerobic activity such as brisk walking, spread over at least 3 days.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Blood pressure control
entities.description: Repeat measurement, lifestyle changes and clinician-guided treatment to reach a target below 130/80 mmHg.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Smoking cessation
entities.description: Counselling and pharmacotherapy to stop tobacco use.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Metformin for diabetes prevention
entities.description: Considered by a clinician for selected high-risk people with prediabetes.

entities.label: Intervention
entities.name: Clinician review and confirmatory testing
entities.description: Professional assessment with laboratory confirmation of glucose status.

evidence.text: Diabetes is diagnosed by an A1C of 6.5% or higher; prediabetes is an A1C of 5.7% to 6.4%.
Diabetes is diagnosed by a fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or higher; prediabetes is a fasting plasma glucose of 100 to 125 mg/dL.
Diabetes is diagnosed by a 2-hour plasma glucose of 200 mg/dL or higher during a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test; prediabetes is 140 to 199 mg/dL.
In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal results from the same sample or two separate samples.
Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes should begin at age 35 for all adults, and earlier in adults with overweight or obesity who have one or more additional risk factors.
Risk factors prompting testing include overweight or obesity, a first-degree relative with diabetes, physical inactivity, and hypertension (blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg or higher, or on therapy).
In Asian American individuals, testing is considered at a lower BMI threshold of 23 kg/m2.
People with prediabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes and should be referred to an intensive lifestyle behavior change program.
Intensive lifestyle intervention reduced the incidence of type 2 diabetes by 58% compared with placebo in adults with impaired glucose tolerance.
Metformin reduced the incidence of type 2 diabetes by 31% compared with placebo, and was less effective than lifestyle intervention.
The lifestyle goals were at least 7% weight loss and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week.
Adults should do at least 150 minutes per week of moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, spread over at least 3 days per week.
A weight loss of 5% or more of body weight can improve glycemia and cardiometabolic risk factors.
Blood pressure should be measured at every routine visit, elevated readings confirmed on a separate day, and the treatment target is below 130/80 mmHg.
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with diabetes, and hypertension is a major contributing risk factor.
All people should be advised not to use cigarettes or other tobacco products, and cessation counselling should be part of care.
Having prediabetes, overweight, being 45 or older, a parent or sibling with type 2 diabetes, and being physically active less than three times a week raise the risk of type 2 diabetes.
Smokers are more likely to develop type 2 diabetes than non-smokers.
Overweight, obesity and physical inactivity are major modifiable factors for type 2 diabetes, and healthy diet, regular activity and avoiding tobacco prevent or delay it.
Diabetes increases the risk of heart attack and stroke, and people with diabetes often also have high blood pressure.
Health care professionals diagnose prediabetes and diabetes using blood tests; a home glucose reading is not a diagnosis.
